problem.text: A loaded tokenizer could retain a serialized truncation policy. Issue #16, “RuntimeError: CUDA error: invalid configuration argument,” reports conversion failure; turboderp attributed it to a tokenizer.json limit of 4096 tokens, insufficient for calibration.

reasoning.text: The constructor now calls self.tokenizer.no_truncation() after loading the backend and auxiliary JSON files, before any vocabulary-probing encodes. This applies the policy once to the shared backend rather than modifying individual encoding calls.

impact.text: The override covers backend encoding used by ordinary and special-token paths, initialization probes, and num_tokens. Wrapper-level BOS/EOS insertion, batch padding and explicit calibration slicing remain unchanged.

Disabling backend truncation preserves input for downstream length management, but can increase tokenization output size and memory use when a serialized limit previously applied. It does not expand model context capacity.

source_notes.text: The connection to issue #16 is inferred from its explicit tokenizer-truncation diagnosis and final comment about overriding the feature at load time, matching this constructor change. DekoMoon reported the failure; turboderp supplied the diagnosis. The discussion is not a locally reproduced conversion result.

Issue #7, “quantizing model: undefined symbol: __cxa_call_terminate,” concerns native-extension loading. Issue #15, “`cogito-v1-preview-qwen-32B` generates incoherent output for bpw <= 2.5,” concerns low-bitrate quantization and regularization. Neither discussion identifies tokenizer truncation as its cause.
The earlier tokenizer entry describes absence-safe BOS/EOS lookup. Those guards remain in the inspected parent and are not changed here.

limitations: No real tokenizers backend, complete tokenizer initialization, conversion or GPU workload was executed. Backend implementation and version-specific API behavior were not independently inspected.
The scalar check models calibration slice lengths only; it neither reproduces the reported CUDA error nor proves conversion succeeds after the change.

chapters.title: Disable inherited tokenizer truncation at load time

claims.text: Tokenizer loads tokenizer.json through HFTokenizer.from_file and reuses that object throughout encoding. The new unconditional no_truncation call overrides backend truncation in memory; it does not rewrite tokenizer files or expose a per-call opt-in.

Calibration's split_raw encodes an entire text before slicing successive column-width rows. get_default_calibration uses this path for code and technical text, with weights 15 and 10 out of a total 128. A backend cap therefore acts before calibration chooses its rows.

A standard-library slice model using the report's 100 rows, 2048 columns and 4096-token cap produced 11 requested code rows and 7 technical rows. Each had only two full slices, with remaining slices empty; full allocations would require 22528 and 14336 tokens respectively.

This supports the reported calibration-shortage mechanism without establishing the CUDA failure chain. Compared with the discussion's alternatives—editing truncation to null or replacing tokenizer.json—the constructor override centralizes the policy and leaves model assets untouched.

annotation.summary: Disable backend tokenizer truncation during construction so serialized limits do not silently shorten inputs before calibration or other encoding consumers.

argv:
weights=[10,15,15,10,48,10,20]; rows=100; cols=2048
for w in (15,10):
 n=max(1,int(w/sum(weights)*rows)); lens=[len(range(4096)[i*cols:(i+1)*cols]) for i in range(n)]
 print({'weight':w,'target_rows':n,'lengths_with_4096_tokens':lens,'tokens_for_full_rows':n*cols})
